newsitem.title: CANADA: Bema, Arizona give Chile results.
newsitem.headline: Bema, Arizona give Chile results.

text.p: Bema Gold Corp and Arizona Star Resource Corp said Thursday that 14 drill holes at their Cerro Casale project had an average grade of 1.24 grams per tonne gold and 0.40 percent copper.
Excluding two higher grade breccia holes, the average grade is 0.92 grams per tonne gold and 0.35 percent copper.
Bema has 49 percent of the project and Arizona Star has 51 percent. Bema controls Arizona Star.
The companies released drill results for four new holes, their first new data on the project since August.

Hole 34 intersected the oxide portion of the main zone between 92 and 216 meters with an average grade of 0.68 grams per tonne gold. From 216 to 440 meters it intersected the sulphide portion of the main porphyry zone with a 224 intercept grading 0.9 grams gold and 0.51 percent copper.
Hole 35 intersected the lower-grade edge of the main porphyry zone from 326 to 472 meters grading 0.4 grams per tonne gold and 0.27 percent copper.
At 472 meters hole 35 intersected the main porphyry zone and an intercept from 472 to 1,016 meters graded 0.95 grams per tonne gold and 0.43 percent copper.

Hole 36 intersected the lower-grade edge of the sulphide portion of the main zone from 410 to 548 meters grading 0.61 grams per tonne gold and 0.25 percent copper. At 549 meters it entered the center of the main porphyry zone and from 549 to 896 meters returned average grades of 0.82 grams per tonne gold and 0.31 percent copper.
Hole 37 hit the main sulphide zone from 260 to 358 meters grading 0.85 grams per tonne gold and 0.43 percent copper.
Between 358 and 522 meters the hole hit a series of low-grade dykes parallel to the hole direction within the porphyry.
Hole 31 and 33 were collared near the northeast edge of the main porphyry zone and defined the northeast extent of the main zone, encountering primarily unmineralized volcanic rock.
Hole 21 was collared 750 meters southwest of the main zone and was drilled to 812 meters. From 628 to 817 meters the grade was 0.47 grams per tonne gold and 0.17 percent copper.

A total of 19 deep holes and 220 shallow holes have now been drilled at Cerro Casale. Of the deep holes, 14 intersected the main porphyry zone which has dimensions of 300 meters wide by 850 meters long and 750 meters deep.

Deep drilling is underway at the property with two rigs. Two more rigs have been sent to the property and will begin drilling next week. The companies said they expect to complete 8 to 10 deep drill holes a month. The focus will be to further confirm the dimensions, grade and continuity of the main porphyry zone, better define the high grade breccia zone and continue step out drilling.
